clue.text: That's in turmoil, with something to strike about at once

indicators.note: a thing in turmoil is thrown into disorder, so the letters get jumbled
about here means going around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: one strikes a pose for the camera
the word taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone in a frantic state, with a weapon to swing, reacting immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike looks like a verb of hitting, but one strikes a pose; the letters of That's are jumbled inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an adverb meaning with all possible speed, immediately, just as the phrase does.

clue.text: Prelude for piano requiring more movement

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters shift around into a new order

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
the word more, rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical instruction: the piano part needs livelier playing in the opening section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks like a section of a symphony, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or introductory passage to a book or speech, which is what a prelude is.

clue.text: Limited calibre of French poet almost taken on board

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut
on board is inside a ship, which crosswords write as two s's around it

blocks.note: Stephane Mallarme, the French symbolist poet
SS stands for steamship; something on board sits between its letters

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark on the modest talent of some French versifier who was nearly let aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: MALLARME loses its last letter and goes inside S...S, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are handheld firearms such as pistols and rifles, weapons whose bore is small.

clue.text: Spacecraft protector manufactured from the halides

indicators.note: something manufactured from raw materials is remade, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A component for space capsules being produced from chemical compounds of halogens.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat shield is the layer on a re-entering capsule that guards it against the extreme temperatures of atmospheric friction.

clue.text: A woman's report on the whole thing

blocks.note: a woman is she; the 's makes the next piece belong to her
a report is the loud sound of a gun going off

explanation.surface: A female journalist's account covering an entire affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' reads as a news story, but here it is the noise of a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole shebang is an idiom for everything involved, the entire business.

clue.text: Former African leader found in the River Test

indicators.note: found in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: Idi Amin, one-time dictator of Uganda
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A deposed dictator turns up in the Test, a famous trout river in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test really is an English river, which disguises it as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine someone is to set them questions as an assessment, the verb sense of test.

clue.text: Drunk is unlikely to buy a round?

definitions.text: is unlikely to buy a round

blocks.note: first meaning: intoxicated

blocks.clueFragment: is unlikely to buy a round
blocks.note: second meaning: stingy with money, as a mean drinker would be

explanation.walkthrough: The surface links the two senses into a pub observation; the second definition describes a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang both for inebriated and for being mean or reluctant to spend money.

clue.text: Touch up what's a bit horny?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to abut is to touch along a border

explanation.surface: A cheeky innuendo about groping something slightly randy.
explanation.walkthrough: The suggestive reading hides a brass instrument: horny here means belonging to the horn family.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba is a large brass wind instrument, loosely one of the horns of an orchestra.

clue.text: Important accent

blocks.note: first meaning: serious, weighty
second meaning: the mark sloping down over a vowel, as in French

explanation.definitionFit: Grave means serious or weighty, and is also the name of the backward-sloping accent mark on letters like e.

clue.text: Jack wants me in durable canvas

blocks.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor
the setter is Paul, so me refers to him
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Jack asks for the setter to be wrapped up in heavy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use me for their own pseudonym; this one signs as Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin is heavy waterproofed cloth, originally tarred canvas, used for covers.

clue.text: Oriental city, huge, with this other name

blocks.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
aka is short for also known as

explanation.surface: A description of a vast Eastern metropolis that also goes by a different title.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan, so a city of the Far East.

clue.text: Premier issue unable to break wind

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart so its letters can be reformed

blocks.note: taken as written
air is a breeze, moving wind

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke about a top-quality child who cannot pass gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue means offspring: Euan is the eldest son of Tony Blair, UK Prime Minister when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of a prime minister is that leader's offspring, and issue is the legal word for children.

clue.text: Trumpeter calls song thrush to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so we do as he would

blocks.note: to dial is to call; this word takes the next word's opening sound
mavis is an old dialect name for the song thrush; it takes the previous word's opening sound

explanation.surface: A trumpet player summoning a songbird, as the famously tongue-tied clergyman might say it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of DIALS MAVIS to hear MILES DAVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Davis was the American jazz musician famous for his trumpet playing.

clue.text: Greek god's wife given a hard time

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An Olympian's spouse being made to suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a hard time' reads as one idiom, but splits into hard and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Olympian deities and the wife of Zeus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Laugh about a boy's sauce

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece sits around the others

blocks.note: something hilarious is a scream
taken as written
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Mocking a young fellow's cheeky backchat.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce reads as impudence in the surface. Salad cream is a tangy British dressing, a cousin of mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a bottled condiment poured over food, a type of sauce.

clue.text: Death produced by coma, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear tells us to take the word coma by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: first meaning: a final departure, leaving this life
second meaning comes from this: a comber, someone using a comb, makes a line in the hair

explanation.surface: A grim medical note on dying after falling unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: Coma sounds like comber, one who combs, and combing hair makes a parting. The medical surface hides the barber.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting is a farewell, euphemistically death, and also the line where hair is combed to either side.

clue.text: Minister's domicile with crime sheet passed round

indicators.note: something passed round another wraps it, putting one piece inside

blocks.note: a page is a sheet of paper
arson is the crime of deliberate fire-raising

explanation.surface: Police circulating a charge sheet about a politician's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Minister suggests a politician, but it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest, a church minister.

clue.text: Gospel member attends church section in recession

indicators.note: recession is a going back, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A congregant goes to services in a part of the church while the economy is shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an archaic word for the gospel, the good news of Christianity, or one of its four books.

clue.text: Come up with, say, design of portico affected by down force

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading the short word from the bottom
a design is a fresh arrangement, so the word that follows is reshaped

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect devises a porch that has to cope with heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down force' sounds like motor racing; it is simply gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Geotropic describes plant growth that responds to gravity, the pull downward toward the earth.

clue.text: Takes stock of the perfect chassis, perhaps? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a car's ideal frame would be free of corrosion

explanation.surface: Someone appraising whether a car's frame is in flawless condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Takes stock reads as reviewing; here stock is livestock, and stealing cattle is rustling.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle or horses, so a rustler literally takes farm livestock.

clue.text: Activate "help" in returned computers, then drag in Yiddish

indicators.note: to activate is to set in motion, so the letters are stirred up
returned means sent back, so the abbreviation is read backwards
in places the stirred letters inside the other piece

blocks.note: PCs are personal computers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Computer instructions: open the help menu on faulty machines, then drag files around.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlep is a word borrowed from Yiddish meaning to haul or carry something heavy and awkward.

clue.text: Body of soldiers overly recruited by draft

indicators.note: something recruited by a group is taken into it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a draft is a preliminary plan
too means excessively

explanation.surface: An army unit that was over-filled by conscription.
explanation.walkthrough: Draft reads as military call-up, but it is an outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of an army company, a small unit of troops.

clue.text: Better to retain second joker

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so one piece keeps the other inside

blocks.note: a better is one who bets, a punter
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Advice that keeping a backup comedian would be an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: Better looks like an adjective, but it is someone who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A punster is someone who makes plays on words, a jokester or wag.

clue.text: "Fish is off", in the Queen's Speech?

indicators.note: we are to hear the word in a cut-glass royal accent, as Her Majesty would pronounce it

blocks.note: a very upper-class pronunciation of off

explanation.surface: An announcement in the monarch's annual address to Parliament that fish has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Speech is the annual royal address opening Parliament; here it means her plummy accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is a freshwater fish related to carp, often kept golden in ornamental ponds.

clue.text: Might one be given a lifelong stretch?

definitions.text: Might one be given a lifelong stretch?

indicators.note: a stretch is a section of something longer, so we take a run of letters from within

blocks.note: the middle run of the word

explanation.surface: A judge musing on who deserves a life sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Stretch is prison slang for a sentence, so the whole clue also describes a criminal serving life.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a person convicted of a serious crime, the kind who could receive a life sentence.

clue.text: Crude stuff is held back by coarse Cornish beast

indicators.note: held back means kept behind, so the first piece trails the other
coarse means rough, suggesting the letters are roughed up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
ore is crude, unrefined mineral

explanation.surface: Some unrefined material is stopped by a rough creature from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: All ten letters of CORNISH plus ORE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is a large horned African or Asian mammal, certainly a beast.

clue.text: A saucy fling?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cheeky, flirtatious affair
setter's reading: a dance that shares its name with a spicy Mexican dip

explanation.walkthrough: Fling is a dance, as in the Highland fling, and saucy hints at a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance and also a tomato-based condiment, so a dance named after a sauce.

clue.text: Viewing restriction where there's filth, it's said

indicators.note: it's said asks us to go by how the phrase is spoken

blocks.note: a pigsty is a filthy place

explanation.surface: A rule about where dirty material may be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests film censorship of smut.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, which can hamper sight.

clue.text: By the sound of it, many people to acquire time-share

indicators.note: this phrase tells us to rely on how the words are spoken
to acquire means taking on, so the last piece is added to the end

blocks.note: a lot means many
men are people
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A timeshare holiday pitch promising large crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Time-share is split: the hyphen hides that time is wordplay and share the definition. An allotment is also a rented British vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a portion allocated to someone, their apportioned part.

clue.text: Throw out old money endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: ex means former
pelf is money, especially ill-gotten

explanation.surface: Discarding obsolete currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force out or eject, as from a school or club.

clue.text: Wise man, one embraced by bird

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside someone's arms

blocks.note: the erne is the sea eagle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sage taken into a bird's embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Wise man suggests a sage, but it is Ernie Wise of Morecambe and Wise, the British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the comedian partnered with Eric Morecambe, so a man surnamed Wise.

clue.text: Microscopic organisms from which a pair came to mutate

indicators.note: to mutate is to change form, so the letters alter their order

blocks.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A biology picture: tiny cells arising when two parents evolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramecia are single-celled ciliate protozoa, visible only under a microscope.
